general.temas: The election campaign, opinion polls and the contest between PSOE and PP dominate several front pages. Sports stories also feature repeatedly, especially Marc Márquez’s title and Alcaraz’s final, as do the failure of the climate summit and the breakdown at Barajas. Only ABC highlights Brussels’ proposal to reduce the number of fishing days in the Mediterranean.
general.motivo_crispacion: The final stretch of the campaign is marked by heightened tension between PSOE and PP, with appeals for tactical voting and confrontational slogans pitting the rival blocs against each other. There is also criticism of Feijóo over contracts awarded by the Xunta, references to judicial interference and an insult in remarks by Rufián. Disagreement between the EU and other countries at the climate summit adds to international tensions. Sports coverage, pensions and service-oriented content provide a calmer counterpoint.

El País.resumen:
- The front page focuses on the November 29 election, with polls, regional analysis and tactical voting tools.
- 40dB.’s tracking poll puts PSOE close behind PP and points to a decline for Vox.
- Sánchez and Feijóo rally their voters in a final stretch of the campaign marked by the battle for first place.
- Gabriel Rufián criticizes party leaderships over the failed left-wing alliance.
- The climate summit ends without the hoped-for agreement on fossil fuels; in sports, Alcaraz faces Zverev in the ATP Finals.
El País.motivo_populismo: Election coverage predominates, although expressions such as “heightens the drama,” “battle” and “sweeps aside,” along with opposing campaign slogans and the quoted insult from Rufián, add emotional and sensationalist weight.
El País.sesgo: The selection prioritizes the electoral contest and tactical voting, with particular attention to the mobilization of the left and PSOE closing the gap with PP. It also covers PP’s messages and Vox’s standing.

El Mundo.resumen:
- A week before the vote, PP and PSOE are gaining support and the right retains its lead, according to the poll presented.
- Campaign coverage also focuses on Formentera, a PP candidate in Gipuzkoa and the prospects of a Sánchez comeback.
- Rufián and Montero call for the right to be stopped and PSOE to be brought to heel after the election.
- The climate summit fails to reach an agreement mentioning fossil fuels; there is also reporting on migrant arrivals in El Hierro and ICE arrests.
- Marc Márquez wins his tenth world title and Barça comes from behind against Villarreal.
El Mundo.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “chaos,” “collapses,” “fiasco” and “send migratory pressure soaring” add drama, although many of the headlines are informative and do not pit the people against the elites.
El Mundo.sesgo: The front page prioritizes the election campaign and devotes several pieces to PP, alongside a critical portrayal of forecasts favorable to Sánchez. On migration, it focuses on pressure on El Hierro and, in the United States, on the methods used by immigration agencies.

ABC.resumen:
- An explosion in a home in Rudilla leaves at least one person dead and two injured.
- Brussels proposes cutting the number of trawling days in the Mediterranean by 32% in 2027.
- Jair Bolsonaro remains in intensive care with an intestinal obstruction.
- A breakdown at Barajas causes overcrowding and difficulties for hundreds of travelers.
- Several sports stories, an interview with La Chispa and articles about Sánchez and Abascal are featured.
ABC.motivo_populismo: Most headlines are informative, although “Dance, you bastards” uses an insulting expression and some sports headlines resort to heightened language.
ABC.sesgo: The front page devotes ample space to sports and combines news with political opinion pieces. One takes a clearly critical view of Sánchez; the excerpt about Abascal does not allow a clear assessment of its stance.

Público.resumen:
- Puigdemont’s entry into the campaign is presented as an offensive against Sánchez to save Junts.
- Left-wing forces seek to mobilize voters; Sánchez predicts historic turnout and ERC puts its faith in Rufián.
- A manifesto by intellectuals denounces the “international oligarchy.”
- The front page addresses judicial actions during the election period and the difficulties a Sánchez government could face.
- A poll puts PP and PSOE level; the front page also questions contracts awarded by the Xunta under Feijóo and the stance of PP and Vox on pensions.
Público.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “finishing blow,” “international oligarchy,” “war footing” and “get tangled up” add drama and confrontation, although some are quotations and other headlines maintain an informative tone.
Público.sesgo: The selection and wording show an approach closer to left-wing forces: they highlight their mobilization efforts and the electoral harm they suffered, while presenting PP and Vox critically. Possible judicial interference is also emphasized, and Feijóo’s conduct at the Xunta is questioned.

OKdiario.resumen:
- Marc Márquez wins another world championship after an injury and celebrates his tenth title with Ducati.
- The front page highlights his age, his tribute in a Barça shirt and his comments about Giacomo Agostini.
- Alcaraz and Zverev face each other in the ATP Finals championship match in Turin.
- Microsoft warns of an Outlook glitch, and the front page reports on the extra pension payment.
- The front page includes culture, cleaning tips and a column about the election.
OKdiario.motivo_populismo: Informative headlines predominate, although expressions such as “makes a habit of epic feats,” “forbidden moves” and “it’s official” add drama and sensationalist appeal, without presenting a confrontation between the people and the elites.
OKdiario.sesgo: The selection shows a clear sports focus, particularly on Marc Márquez, and combines service journalism with entertainment. The election column takes an opinionated tone on voting, but the excerpt does not allow it to be attributed to any particular party-political orientation.

opiniones.comunista:
In the final stretch of the campaign, we are being invited to calculate our tactical vote as though politics were only a matter of seats. I believe the decisive question is another: who will have the power to decide what happens to the wealth produced by the working class? A tax on banks can fund public services, but it is not enough if credit and investment remain subordinated to private profit. I support public banking and collective ownership of strategic sectors, under democratic control.

The failure of the climate summit also shows the limits of leaving the future in the hands of those who depend on fossil fuels. We need a planned transition that reduces their use, guarantees decent jobs and protects workers. Without collective power, election promises risk remaining just promises.
opiniones.anarquista:
The campaign turns our ability to decide into a narrow question: which party benefits most from our vote. I would rather ask what we gain by delegating every few years to organizations that aspire to govern us from above. Promises of taxes or new laws may distinguish the candidates, but they are no substitute for people’s power to organize their own lives.

The failure of the climate summit also shows the limits of entrusting our shared future to negotiations between states. Faced with dependence on fossil fuels, I support communities and workers who can decide how to produce and consume, through self-management and mutual aid. Freedom is not just about choosing representatives: it requires the ability to act alongside others, without obeying political or economic hierarchies.
opiniones.liberal:
Amid the polls and calls for tactical voting, I miss a fundamental question: how much room will the next government leave for each citizen to make decisions about their life and their money? The promise of new taxes on banks deserves a serious debate about their potential costs for customers, investment and competition, not just campaign applause.

I prefer low taxes and stable rules that allow people to start businesses, save and take risks. A limited state should protect rights, guarantee competition and perform its functions well, not turn every problem into an excuse to expand its power. That also requires personal responsibility: freedom does not exempt us from answering for our decisions.

The failure of the climate summit is a reminder of another real challenge. Addressing it requires cooperation and incentives to innovate, without assuming that more intervention is always the best answer.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I worry that the campaign is being reduced to polls and tactical voting calculations, while essential decisions are pushed aside. Spain needs to regain control of its borders: the arrival of six cayucos in El Hierro calls for a firm policy against illegal immigration and sufficient resources to protect our coasts. Security and compliance with the law are non-negotiable.

I also reject Brussels’ proposal to cut fishing days without prioritizing those who sustain a trade and a way of life rooted in our communities. Sustainability matters, but it cannot be an excuse to decide the future of the Spanish fleet from afar. I want representatives who defend national sovereignty and our traditions, not leaders preoccupied with headlines and opinion polls.
opiniones.centro:
A week before the election, I would not confuse polls with the result or a tactical vote with a blank check. Competition between PP and PSOE is legitimate, but the confrontational tone should give way to verifiable commitments: how to sustain pensions, fund public services and respect the independence of institutions. A tax on banks deserves to be debated on its effects and its revenue-raising capacity, not just its electoral appeal.

I am also concerned about the failure of the climate summit. The transition must recognize the role of fossil fuels, but it needs realistic timelines and support for those who face higher costs. I believe in a market economy capable of innovation, accompanied by social protection that shares the burden fairly. Without broad agreements, reforms will last less time than the problems they seek to solve.
